hotspots.fact: UNEP's Ogoniland assessment found families drinking well water with benzene, a known carcinogen, at over 900 times the WHO guideline.
An independent assessment estimated that 103,000 to 311,000 barrels of oil leaked into Bodo Creek over 72 days in 2008, against Shell's own figure of 1,640 barrels.

hotspots.loc_basis: Agbabu populated place, GeoNames (listed under Okitipupa LGA)
hotspots.fact: A study of water sources in Ondo's bitumen belt recorded total petroleum hydrocarbons up to 1,480 mg/L in a Lodasa well and 900 mg/L in the Agbabu stream.

hotspots.n: Bagega and Dareta lead poisoning (artisanal gold mining)
hotspots.fact: An estimated 400 children died of lead poisoning from gold-ore processing before MSF's intervention began in June 2010, and about 1,500 children in Bagega were still exposed in 2012 (exposure was mainly through dust and soil; UNEP's 2010 mission also sampled ground and surface water).

hotspots.loc_basis: Kagara, the Rafi LGA headquarters (GeoNames); Shikira village itself was not located, so treat this as an approximate LGA marker
hotspots.fact: Health officials reported 65 cases of lead poisoning and 28 child deaths linked to illegal gold mining in Shikira and nearby communities.

hotspots.loc_basis: An Enyigba populated place in Ebonyi State, GeoNames; GeoNames lists three places with this name, so the choice is uncertain
hotspots.fact: Stream water and groundwater in the Enyigba lead-zinc mining communities exceeded Nigerian drinking-water and WHO thresholds for aluminium, iron and lead.
Downstream of effluent discharges, River Challawa had cadmium, chromium, lead and nickel above WHO guideline limits, and turbidity of about 168 NTU against a limit of 25 NTU.

hotspots.loc_basis: Romi populated place (Chikun LGA), GeoNames; a GeoNames point on the River Romi itself is at 10.4905, 7.3407
hotspots.fact: Below the Kaduna refinery discharge point, oil and grease in the Romi River rose from 2.7 to 4.7 mg/L, and lead, cadmium and chromium exceeded NESREA and WHO standards.

hotspots.place: Ikeja industrial area (flows to Lagos Lagoon)
hotspots.loc_basis: No coordinate found on any page I opened
hotspots.fact: Sediments at the upstream point receiving the most industrial effluent held the highest metal levels (lead 108.3, zinc 805, cadmium 42.1), far above levels further downstream.
The lagoon receives effluent from the Agbara Industrial Estate, and its sediments were rated highly polluted with manganese (Igeo 4.1 to 5.8) and strongly polluted with zinc.
The Ogunpa River's water quality index was 2,384 in the dry season and 1,144 in the wet season, and the copper ingestion hazard index reached 14.8.
Total organochlorine pesticides in the river reached 12.28 µg/L upstream, about 24 times the 0.5 µg/L limit the authors cite.

hotspots.loc_basis: Aba city (Aba South LGA seat), GeoNames
hotspots.fact: Abattoir and industrial wastes left the Aba River with faecal and total coliform counts above allowable limits, and water at the abattoir station was acidic (pH 5.9).
In a cholera outbreak with 6 deaths, cases were about 14 times more likely than controls to have drunk from the Zamani River (OR 14.2).
